method.value: Non-LTE spherically symmetric radiative transfer of outflows to compare predicted line strength with observed

evidence.quote: we used GASTRoNOoM (cite: Decin2006) to calculate non-LTE spherically-symmetric radiative transfer models for the outflows of the five sources.

key_parameters.value: initial expansion velocity 2 km/s; stellar temperature 3000 K

evidence.quote: We adopt an initial expansion velocity, $\upsilon(R_\circ) = \upsilon_\circ$, of 2 km/s.
we have not considered emission from the outflow when fitting the observations.

method.value: Spherical WML radiative transfer with constant density and vibrational temperature; stellar radius from ALMA continuum; line-of-sight intensity integration

evidence.quote: We opt for a simple model in which the density, $n_{\rm WML}$, and excitation temperature of CO, $T^{\rm Vib}_{\rm WML}$, are constant throughout the WML.

key_parameters.value: T_vib = 1000, 1500, 2000 K; free: R_o, n_WML, velocity dispersion, global radial velocity

evidence.quote: We calculated models with $T^{\rm Vib}_{\rm WML}$ equal to 1000 K, 1500 K, and 2000 K.

assumptions.value: Stellar temperature 3000 K blackbody; companion ignored

evidence.quote: We have not considered the presence of a companion star in our calculations.

fitting.value: 1 sigma uncertainties from mapping chi2 around best model for inverse P-Cygni profiles; from line flux uncertainty for o Cet and W Aql

evidence.quote: we obtained the $1\sigma$ uncertainties from mapping the $\chi^{2}$ around the best model
we used GASTRoNOoM (cite: Decin2006) to calculate non-LTE spherically-symmetric radiative transfer models

results_numeric.quantity: o Cet peak flux density, 2014-02-25 to 2014-05-03

evidence.quote: the peak flux density increases from 0.15 Jy close to minimum-light phase to 0.40 Jy close to maximum-light phase

results_numeric.quantity: Max fraction of WML mass lost per pulsation cycle, o Cet

evidence.quote: $\lesssim 1.0\%$ for $o$ Cet and $\lesssim 7.5\%$ for W Aql

findings_qualitative.value: R Aqr and R Scl show inverse P-Cygni profiles indicating infall; o Cet and R Scl show line variability

evidence.quote: R Aqr and R Scl show inverse P-Cygni line profiles which indicate infall of material onto the stars.

claims.hypothesis: Vibrationally excited CO rotational lines are detectable with ALMA towards AGB stars and trace the WML
claims.experiment: Serendipitous detection in five stars and simple WML radiative transfer fits
claims.result: Line detected in 5 of 5 sources; fitted with constant-density WML models
claims.finding: Such lines can be observed towards many nearby AGB stars

evidence.quote: The serendipitous detection towards these five sources shows that vibrationally-excited rotational lines can be observed towards a large number of nearby AGB stars using ALMA.

claims.hypothesis: Lines indicate infall in some stars
claims.result: Models require infalling gas for R Aqr and R Scl
claims.finding: Material falls back onto the stars

evidence.quote: Our models require the gas in the WMLs to be falling back to the stars, as expected from the line profiles.

limitations_admitted.value: Uncertainties reflect only the fitting; systematic errors from model assumptions can be larger

evidence.quote: the systematic errors from our model assumptions can be larger than those.

referee_caveats_inferred: Simple constant-density spherical model with strong parameter degeneracy
Mass-loss rates highly uncertain for R Aqr and R Scl
